Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Verdant's security team reviewed the integration and we have two asks before procurement can approve:

1) We need a SIG/CAIQ mapping focused on log retention, deletion workflows, and evidence artifacts you can provide for SOC 2/ISO audits (a spreadsheet is fine).
2) For a narrow trial period (90 days), Verdant would like Redwood to retain expanded debug/trace logs for the Verdant tenant to support live forensics for a new feature rollout. This would be a tenant-scoped exception — volume will be modest.

Can you confirm operational impact, whether this is feasible in Hosted or Dedicated, and what compensating controls/redlines you would need? We also need an estimated timeline to deliver the SIG mapping and any redline language for the contract.

I've attached our formal request packet. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll review whether Hosted can be scoped for a tenant-specific retention extension; Dedicated is more straightforward operationally.

Would Verdant accept a 90-day exception that is: tenant-scoped, timeboxed (start/end dates), audited with read-only access to snapshots delivered to the customer’s S3, and limited to traces flagged for forensics (not full traffic)? If yes, please confirm and we'll prepare the draft.

Priya / Karthik — I reviewed Verdant's packet. Operational notes and proposed controls below.

Operational feasibility:
- Hosted: We can implement tenant-scoped extended retention as a config flag but it requires a short feature gate and QA; risk surface is low if we restrict write paths. Delivery ETA: ~7-10 business days to deploy and validate in production.
- Dedicated: We can apply the retention policy at the node/instance level immediately for customers on Dedicated pools — near-immediate (1-2 business days) with DBA coordination.

Proposed compensating controls for 90-day exception:
- Scoped TTL: Only debugging/tracing topics with a specific tag (verdant_forensics=true) retained for 90 days. Default telemetry remains unchanged.
- Access controls: SAML/SCIM-based access, RBAC for the retention snapshot job — only Verdant and Redwood Security.
- Snapshot delivery: Daily encrypted snapshots of the retained subset pushed to Verdant's pre-provisioned S3 bucket; server-side encryption + dedicated KMS key.
- Audit trail & attestations: System audit logs for any retention toggles and snapshot pulls; we provide a signed attestation at the end of the 90-day window.
- Sampling and redaction: PII masking rules applied during snapshot generation; full PII erasure path post-window.

Contract language (draft bullet):
- "Redwood agrees to a tenant-scoped, timeboxed retention extension for Verdant Biosys (Start: <mm/dd/yyyy>, End: <mm/dd/yyyy>) limited to debug traces explicitly flagged by Verdant. Redwood will provide daily encrypted snapshots and maintain audit logs of all retention-related operations. Verdant retains the right to terminate the exception early and request proof-of-delete for snapshot artifacts."

SIG/CAIQ mapping deliverable plan:
- 48h: Spreadsheet mapping SIG questions related to Logging & Retention -> list of artifacts we can provide (SOC2 test reports, audit log extracts, KMS usage logs, retention config snapshots).
- 3 days: Operational runbook & retention matrix (.csv) and compensating-controls doc for contract team to review.

I'll assemble the artifacts and push to the shared Drive link; Priya, can you confirm the requested start date so I can populate the contract language?

—Ben
